Notes

变坏

变坏 biàn huài means “become bad”; 变态 biàn tài means abnormal or warped and can also be an insult meaning “pervert.” The line proposes a grim alternative: become bad now or become twisted later. Repeating 变 makes the turn almost sound like a correction.

  • Genius community transcript
乖

乖 is the approving word used for someone well-behaved or compliant, especially a child. Applied to an animal that was nevertheless slaughtered, the approval becomes useless. It supplies the passage’s concrete argument for the earlier demand to “turn bad”: being good did not keep this creature safe.

  • Genius community transcript
目是死不冥的

This line reshapes 死不瞑目, “die without closing one’s eyes”: to die with an unresolved grievance or regret. The community text prints 冥 where the idiom normally uses 瞑. The Chinese is preserved as supplied; the next line’s explicit regret supports translating the idiom rather than treating that spelling as a new image.

  • Genius community transcript
头号

The community transcript prints 头号, “number one” or “top-ranked,” which sits awkwardly in this sentence. “Top billing” retains that wording in the English draft. The larger accusation is clear—someone trades on what belongs to the speaker to deceive people—but the exact noun needs checking against the recording.

  • Genius community transcript
招摇撞骗

招摇撞骗 means deceive people by bluffing, showing off a supposed position or trading on a name. It is more specific than merely telling lies. Although the preceding noun is unclear in the transcript, the accusation is that someone converts a claimed association with the speaker into credibility for a scam.

  • Genius community transcript
看我的脸色

看脸色 means watch someone’s mood and adjust your behavior accordingly. 脸色 is also the visible look or color of a face. The next line turns that social deference into a corpse joke: a dead person cannot offer a welcoming look, and does not have a healthy complexion either.

  • Genius community transcript
黑锅你愿意背

背黑锅 means be made a scapegoat or take blame, literally “carry the black pot.” Here the question puts a price on claiming brotherhood: will the would-be brother actually take the fall? It develops the same carrying-blame image heard in “Self Pity.”

  • Genius community transcript
以泪洗面

以泪洗面 is a set expression for weeping continually: tears become the water that washes the face. The later instructions to get up and discard the baby bottle extend the image into a rebuke against helplessness. The very last “I hope I’m right” then makes the promised recovery less certain than those commands sound.

  • Genius community transcript
